items.title: Report: FTC probes Anthropic, OpenAI after Trump dismissed AI fears as “hoax”
items.excerpt: The FTC sent 50-plus-page civil investigative demands to OpenAI and Anthropic seeking documents on recent AI security incidents, safeguarding practices, marketing and privacy policies, in a consumer-protection probe first reported by Axios; the agency could seek penalties comparable to those for delayed data-breach disclosure.

items.title: Exclusive: AI safety money floods into political races
items.excerpt: AI safety groups and individual donors, including researchers at OpenAI and Redwood, have spent about $48 million this US election cycle on Democratic and Republican candidates who favor AI regulation, per figures shared with Axios; Guardrails Alliance, a tech-worker-backed group, has raised $11.7 million.

items.title: UK Election Watchdog Develops AI System to Flag Deepfakes Within 3 Hours
items.excerpt: The UK Electoral Commission is developing an AI system that scans social media in near real time and flags significant deepfakes so staff can alert affected candidates within three hours; a May 2026 local-election pilot analysed about 3 million posts, flagged 147 and referred 10 to platforms or police.

items.title: Meta Moderation Failures Loom Over Brazil’s Runoff Presidential Election
items.excerpt: Ahead of Brazil's presidential runoff, Tech Policy Press reports Meta AI's image generator produced images of Jair Bolsonaro but refused to depict Lula for users in Brazil (while doing so via VPN), alongside complaints about bias in Meta AI outputs and restricted users.

items.title: Multiple Polls Find Most Americans Think AI is Moving Too Fast
items.excerpt: Five polls from major pollsters find most Americans think AI is moving too fast, with Democrats more wary than Republicans - a public-opinion backdrop to the AI regulation fight ahead of the US midterms.

items.title: Trump posts AI-edited photo to brag about White House restoration work
items.excerpt: President Trump posted an AI-edited image to tout restoration work at the White House, the latest instance of the president sharing AI-altered imagery on official channels.

items.title: Nobody is safe from celebrity AI deepfakes
items.excerpt: AI-generated likenesses of celebrities are proliferating on Instagram, and Meta does not require labels for AI-generated still images - a gap in platform AI-labeling policy that also applies to public figures.

items.title: UK keeps AI safeguards in the maybe pile for Cyber Security BIll
items.excerpt: Senior UK civil servants told MPs the government is still considering AI-specific amendments to the Cyber Security and Resilience Bill, stopping short of committing despite ministers' pledge to legislate where needed amid warnings about autonomous AI threats.

items.title: UK government chases AI while aging IT leaves it exposed, PAC chair warns
items.excerpt: Public Accounts Committee chair Sir Geoffrey Clifton-Brown's annual report warns Whitehall is pushing AI ambitions while failing to replace aging IT, as AI gives criminals and hostile states new attack routes: 'AI is approaching government like a tsunami.'

items.title: Europe’s leaders abandon the race for frontier AI
items.excerpt: European politicians and tech executives are shifting away from competing on frontier AI models with the US and China, with a new mantra that Europe need not own the models as long as it can deploy them.

items.title: EU’s cyber unit turns to AI to fend off ‘high-risk’ hacks
items.excerpt: An internal European Commission IT-department document obtained by POLITICO sets out an action plan to use AI to respond to high-risk cyberattacks and prepare EU executive defenses for 'emerging AI-driven threats'.

items.title: MI5 to step up on AI threats amid bioweapon risk
items.excerpt: MI5 Director General Ken McCallum announced in his annual threat update that the agency has set up an AI Threat Assessment Centre to shape how the UK government assesses AI-enabled state, terrorist and other national-security threats.

items.title: France carves its own path in AI race with Nvidia’s help
items.excerpt: France is pushing for AI sovereignty with Nvidia's help as the chipmaker bets almost $10 billion in Europe, positioning Paris as an alternative to the US-China AI race.

items.title: AI Hacks Leave a Mess That AI Companies Aren’t Paying For
items.excerpt: Despite a string of incidents in which AI models and agents caused harm - including Anthropic's false murder tip to Philadelphia police - targets are rarely seeking legal redress, leaving AI companies largely free of liability.

items.title: AI Models Can Be Easily Modified to Assist Terrorist and Extremist Activity
items.excerpt: Researchers found open-weight AI models with guardrails removed readily provide detailed assistance for terrorist and extremist activity, sharpening the policy debate over releasing open models.

items.title: OpenAI, Google pushing new AI models easily tricked into making nudes, researchers say
items.excerpt: Researchers say an attack method easily tricks new OpenAI and Google image models into producing nude images, exposing flaws in safeguards against non-consensual AI nudes that lawmakers have targeted.

items.title: AI labs are buying data from dead startups to train their models
items.excerpt: A new industry is brokering data from failed startups to AI labs for model training, raising privacy and consent questions over what happens to user data when companies die.

items.title: An AI company wanted to buy my reporting notes.
items.excerpt: A journalist recounts a 'data procurement worker' offering to buy reporters' notes and interview transcripts for AI training - a window into the data-licensing market behind AI models.

items.title: First Lady Melania Trump Launches 2027 Presidential SI Challenge and Establishes First Lady Seal of SI Readiness
items.excerpt: First Lady Melania Trump launched the 2027 Presidential Super Intelligence (SI) Challenge and a First Lady Seal of SI Readiness, extending the administration's AI-education push under its 'super intelligence' branding.

items.title: The UAE embraces AI for kindergartners
items.excerpt: The UAE has mandated AI education from kindergarten through 12th grade, offering a glimpse of national AI-literacy policy if AI becomes as fundamental as reading and writing.
